items.symptom: Melee / short-range bullets never hit
items.cause: a row with life = range / speed under one frame (Zeus: 3 m at 2000 m/s = 1.5 ms) dies before the engine collides it; a melee row shorter than your target acceptance falls short.

items.cause: decals were placed at the marker even with no map surface there, and the character-hit report can arrive after the impact marker.

items.cause: the replacement model only drew with a depth copy from this or the last frame.

items.symptom: 3D models either hidden under the ImGui menus or drawn over the HUD
items.cause: hudhook 0.9.3's DX12 backend has no hook around its ImGui pass.

items.symptom: VRF-exported clips double the root transform
items.cause: a standalone clip export keeps glTF's Z-up → Y-up turn on `root_motion`, while a model export with `--gltf_animation_list` bakes it into the root's children.

items.symptom: Additive world clips used as poses give A-pose arms
items.detail: VRF composes additive clips over the bind pose (`--gltf_compose_additive`); apply them relative to their first frame, never as a full pose.

items.symptom: Particles with tinted sprites look dark
items.cause: the additive pass multiplies colour by alpha, so textures baked premultiplied lose it twice.

items.symptom: A small screen texture (Zeus charge digits) blurs
items.cause: a 7-segment display draws every segment from one texture column with its own row; mips merge the rows.

items.symptom: Case odds felt rigged
items.cause: the RNG was seeded from `Instant::now().elapsed()` (≈ 0, same seed every time).

items.symptom: The death screen named a long-dead enemy after a fall
items.cause: `last_hit_by` keeps the last attacker forever.

items.symptom: The level-up undo looks like it might fight the game
items.detail: It doesn't, if you restore the previous tick's level, attributes, both PlayerGameData maxima and the ChrIns data-module maxima, and refund the rune delta of that same tick.

items.cause: the GL backend's depth `copyTextureToBuffer` sets the read FBO's read buffer to `GL_NONE` and never restores it.

items.symptom: Setup commands on join match nobody (`@a` is empty)
items.cause: Fabric's `ServerPlayConnectionEvents.JOIN` fires before the player is in the player list.

items.cause: GTA's pause menu stops ScriptHookV scripts, so nothing clears the overlay.

items.detail: Cause: baking every frame of every clip at full rate. Fix: thin frames (every second or third) and let the renderer interpolate; share animations between skin variants.

items.detail: Cause: a record size or field offset is off by a few bytes. Fix: print the next record's name string after every struct walk; a wrong size fails loudly at the second record.

items.cause: exports are stored in reverse declaration order.

items.symptom: Keep everything local:
items.detail: decompressed packages, dumps and the `.jar` are game data. Git-ignore them. Publish only your scripts and notes.

items.symptom: Black frames
items.detail: GDI/`gdigrab` can't see GPU-rendered games. Use gfxcapture (or `ddagrab` for the whole monitor).

items.symptom: Empty .mkv, and ffmpeg ignores 'q'
items.cause: gfxcapture only delivers a frame when the window redraws. A paused game, static menu or minimized window produces nothing, and ffmpeg is stuck waiting.

items.symptom: Never stop ffmpeg from the game's main thread
items.detail: If the game blocks, gfxcapture stalls and the 'q' is never read. The tail of the take is lost.

items.symptom: NVENC H.264 is limited to 4096 px wide
items.detail: Crop 32:9 screens to the centre 16:9, scale down, or use HEVC.

items.symptom: Reading the back buffer from inside the game can leak
items.detail: FNA3D's D3D11 `ReadBackbuffer` allocated a staging texture per call (17 GB in one take). Capture from outside.

items.symptom: The game's audio can't be redirected
items.detail: Many engines (FAudio, Unity, Unreal) talk to WASAPI directly, so SDL/driver tricks do nothing. Use process loopback.

items.symptom: Audio a few hundred ms early
items.detail: ffmpeg + capture + encoder startup takes about 0.25-0.3 s before the first frame. Account for it in the mux, and measure once per machine.
